## Alternative proofs

### logic:aca-equivalents — Direct construction of arithmetical sets via a universal Σ^{0}_{1} normal form and the jump

**Idea.** Instead of a metalevel induction on formula complexity, show that 2 (Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension) gives, for every set parameter Y, a set coding the halting problem relative to Y, i.e. the jump Y'; then observe that every arithmetical formula with set parameters is Δ^{0}_{2} in those parameters, hence its extension is computed from finitely many iterated jumps, which exist by iterating 2. This is essentially the standard equivalence of ACA_{0} with 'every set has a jump' (Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, II.3 / VIII.1), but the direction 'jump ⇒ arithmetical comprehension' can be run purely combinatorially without formalizing the enumeration theorem, by coding bounded quantifier blocks as finite iterations of Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension.

1. Step 1 — Jump exists: For any set Y, the set Y'={(e,n) : ∃s T^{Y}(e,n,s)} (T^{Y} the relativized Kleene T-predicate, a bounded-in-s formula with Y-parameters) exists by Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension. (Definition of the jump; T^{Y} is Δ^{0}_{0} in Y.)
2. Step 2 — Iterating comprehension: By primitive recursion on k using Step 1, the finite iterates Y^{(k)} exist for every k. (Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension applied k times; the recursion is on the index, so no comprehension on sets of sets is needed.)
3. Step 3 — Bounded quantifiers are decidable from a jump: For a Δ^{0}_{0} formula θ, both ∃m θ(m,n) and ∀m θ(m,n) are Σ^{0}_{1} in the parameters, hence their extensions exist by 2. (Immediate from the definition of Σ^{0}_{1}.)
4. Step 4 — Arithmetical formulas are Δ^{0}_{2} in the parameters: Every arithmetical formula with set parameters is equivalent to a Boolean combination of Σ^{0}_{2} formulas, and a Σ^{0}_{2} formula ∃m∀l θ is Σ^{0}_{1} relative to the jump of the parameters. (Classical normal form; provable by induction on the formula, using that a bounded quantifier applied to a Σ^{0}_{1} formula is again Σ^{0}_{1}.)
5. Step 5 — Conclusion: Combining Steps 2 and 4, every arithmetical formula with parameters has a defining set, i.e. arithmetical comprehension holds. (Apply 2 to the Σ^{0}_{1}-in-Y' description obtained in Step 4.)

**Prerequisites.** Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension (item 2), the Kleene T-predicate and its elementary properties, and the normal form theorem for arithmetical formulas. Heavier than the given proof in computability-theoretic background, lighter in proof-theoretic bookkeeping (no induction on derivations).

**Why instructive.** It makes explicit the remark on the page that 2 is equivalent to 'every set has a jump', and shows concretely why one jump suffices for all arithmetical comprehension: arithmetical formulas are exactly those decidable from finitely many jumps.

### logic:aca-analysis — Specker-style direct reduction: encode the range of an injection into a bounded monotone sequence and read it off by a Π^{0}_{1} test

**Idea.** The given proof of 5⇒1 already uses the Specker sequence; an essentially different route to the cycle is to prove 1⇒5 directly by a bisection/least-upper-bound argument on the rationals rather than via 4, and to derive 5⇒4 by a direct construction of the supremum as the limit of the monotone sequence of truncated maxima. This reorganizes the cycle as 1⇒5⇒4⇒3⇒2⇒5, avoiding the separate 'supremum from Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension' argument and the nested-interval argument for Bolzano–Weierstrass, replacing the latter by 'bounded sequence has a monotone subsequence' (Erdős–Szekeres, provable in RCA_{0}).

1. Step 1 — 1⇒5: Given a bounded increasing sequence (x_{n}) with |x_{n}|≤b, the set S={(k,j) : ∃n (x_{n}>j2^{-k})} exists by Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension; define s_{k}=max{j2^{-k} : -b2^{k}≤j≤b2^{k}, (k,j)∈S}. Then (s_{k}) is a real s and s=lim x_{n}. (Same computation as the given 1⇒4, Steps 1–4, but only the 'limit' half is used.)
2. Step 2 — 5⇒4: For a bounded sequence (x_{n}), the sequence y_{n}=max_{i≤n}x_{i} exists by bounded comprehension and is increasing and bounded, so by 5 it has a limit s; then s is the least upper bound of (x_{n}). (Bounded comprehension in RCA_{0}; the max is primitive recursive.)
3. Step 3 — 4⇒3: For a Cauchy sequence (x_{n}), the sequence y_{n}=x_{n}-2^{-n} is bounded below and its supremum s (by 4) satisfies |x_{n}-s|≤2^{-n+1}, so s=lim x_{n}. (Standard 'sup of x_{n}-2^{-n}' trick; uses only the definition of supremum and the Cauchy property.)
4. Step 4 — 3⇒2: A bounded sequence (x_{n}) has a monotone subsequence (Erdős–Szekeres: define n_{k} to be the least index after n_{k-1} that is a 'record high' or a 'record low'; one of the two cases must occur infinitely often). A bounded monotone subsequence is Cauchy, hence converges by 3. (Erdős–Szekeres lemma provable in RCA_{0} by bounded comprehension and primitive recursion.)
5. Step 5 — 2⇒5: A bounded increasing sequence is bounded, so by 2 it has a convergent subsequence; as in the given proof, the limit of the subsequence is the limit of the sequence. (Same argument as the given 2⇒5.)
6. Step 6 — 5⇒1: As in the given proof, the Specker sequence c_{n}=Σ_{i≤n}2^{-f(i)} for an injection f is bounded and increasing, so has a limit c; the range of f is Δ^{0}_{1}-definable from c, hence exists by Δ^{0}_{1} comprehension. (Identical to the given 5⇒1.)

**Prerequisites.** Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension, bounded comprehension in RCA_{0}, the Erdős–Szekeres monotone subsequence lemma, Δ^{0}_{1} comprehension. Comparable to the given proof; it replaces the nested-interval theorem by Erdős–Szekeres.

**Why instructive.** It shows that the cycle can be closed using only one 'hard' direction (1⇒5, the Specker computation) plus soft combinatorial steps, making clear that the strength of completeness lies entirely in the monotone convergence theorem and that Bolzano–Weierstrass, Cauchy completeness and the supremum principle are cheap consequences of it.

## Alternative definitions

### logic:aca-equivalents (equivalent)

ACA_{0} is equivalent over RCA_{0} to: for every set X there exists its Turing jump X' = {e : the e-th program with oracle X halts on input e}.

**Conditions.** Over RCA_{0}; requires a formalization of the relativized Kleene T-predicate and the enumeration theorem in RCA_{0}.

**Equivalence.** X' is Σ^{0}_{1} in X, so ACA_{0} gives it by Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension. Conversely, every arithmetical formula in a parameter X is Δ^{0}_{2} in X, hence decidable from X' (and finitely many iterates of the jump, which exist by iterating the hypothesis); so arithmetical comprehension follows. This is the 'jump closure' characterization of ω-models of ACA_{0} (Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, VIII.1).

**Reference.** S. G. Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, 2nd ed., Springer (2009), Chapter VIII; the page's own remark 1.

### logic:aca-equivalents (equivalent)

ACA_{0} is equivalent over RCA_{0} to: the range of every function f: N→N exists (not only of injections).

**Conditions.** Over RCA_{0}.

**Equivalence.** The direction 'ranges of all functions ⇒ Σ^{0}_{1} comprehension' is immediate since {n : ∃m f(m)=n} is Σ^{0}_{1} in f; the converse is item 2⇒3 of the theorem, which does not use injectivity. Hence restricting to injections does not weaken the principle, as the page's supplement notes.

**Reference.** The page's supplement; S. G. Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, II.3.

### logic:konig-lemma-def (NOT equivalent)

A variant: KL' = 'every infinite tree T⊆N^{<N} in which every node has at most two children has a path'. This is NOT equivalent to KL over RCA_{0}; it is strictly stronger (equivalent to ACA_{0}).

**Conditions.** Over RCA_{0}; the equivalence with KL fails because KL' does not require a uniform bound on the labels of children.

**Equivalence.** KL⇒KL' is trivial (at most two children is finite branching). KL'⇒ACA_{0} is item 3⇒1 of logic:konig-aca. The bounded-label version ('children bounded by a function h of the length') is equivalent to WKL over RCA_{0}, as in problem logic:prob-bounded-konig-wkl; the failure of equivalence is exactly the absence of such an h.

**Reference.** The page's remark after logic:konig-aca; S. G. Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, III.7 (weak König's lemma and bounded König's lemma).

### logic:rm-analysis-defs (equivalent)

A real number s is the supremum of (x_{n}) iff s is an upper bound and for every rational ε>0 there is n with x_{n}>s-ε (equivalently, s is the least upper bound in the sense that any upper bound t satisfies s≤t).

**Conditions.** Over RCA_{0}, for bounded sequences; the 'least upper bound' formulation and the 'approximation from below by 2^{-k}' formulation are equivalent.

**Equivalence.** If s is least and some k had x_{n}≤s-2^{-k} for all n, then s-2^{-k} would be a smaller upper bound; conversely if s is approximated from below and t<s is an upper bound, choose k with 2^{-k}<s-t and n with x_{n}>s-2^{-k}>t, contradicting that t is an upper bound. The uniqueness of the supremum then follows in RCA_{0}.

**Reference.** The page's definition logic:rm-analysis-defs; S. G. Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, II.6 (real numbers).

## Other notes

The page is in good shape; all proof steps already carry 【主張】-style labels, so the step_claims above are mostly confirmations of the existing content (the source shows no explicit 【主張：...】 markers, so they are listed as new). Two small improvements: (1) In logic:aca-analysis, the proof of 1⇒4 Step 2 writes a_{k}=max{...} over a finite set of candidates; it would help to say explicitly that this maximum is obtained by bounded comprehension plus the least-number principle, since 'max over a finite set' is not a primitive of RCA_{0}. (2) In logic:range-injection-sigma01 Step 3, the equivalence '∃k f(k)=2n+1 iff some m is least with θ(·,n)' deserves one extra sentence: the odd value 2n+1 is attained exactly at k=(m,n) with m least, and the least-number principle for bounded formulas is available in RCA_{0}. (3) The hypcheck mentions '有界収集の原理 (IΣ_{1})' in the context of Σ^{0}_{1} induction; it would be clearer to state that Σ^{0}_{1} induction is available in RCA_{0} and that the bounded collection used is provable from it.
